iconic_games_note: Arrowhead is primarily an NFL stadium but has a genuine (if modest) association-football history: it was home to MLS charter club the Kansas City Wiz/Wizards (now Sporting Kansas City) from 1996 to 2007, and it hosted USMNT and CONCACAF Gold Cup fixtures over the years. Its most notable single football match is the 2024 Copa América Group C tie listed above (USA 0–1 Uruguay, 1 Jul 2024, att. 55,460), making it one of the venues to host both the Copa América and the FIFA World Cup. Its biggest events overall are NFL/Chiefs games — American football, not association football — including the Guinness-record crowd-noise game.

city_history.founded: Incorporated as the Town of Kansas in 1850; reincorporated as the City of Kansas in 1853 and renamed Kansas City in 1889
city_history.significance: Largest city in Missouri, on the Missouri–Kansas state line at the confluence of the Missouri and Kansas rivers. A historic rail, stockyard and commerce hub of the American Midwest, it is internationally known for its jazz heritage (the 18th & Vine district), Kansas City-style barbecue, and its fountains. The metro straddles two states (Missouri and Kansas).
city_history.football_culture: Kansas City is a deep football (soccer) town for its size: it is the home of MLS's Sporting Kansas City — a charter MLS club (founded 1996 as the Kansas City Wiz/Wizards) that played at Arrowhead through 2007 before moving to its own soccer-specific stadium — and of the NWSL's Kansas City Current, who built the first stadium purpose-built for a women's professional team. The city hosted the 2024 Copa América and multiple USMNT and Gold Cup fixtures. (Separately, on the gridiron, the NFL's Chiefs make Arrowhead one of the loudest venues in sport.)

sources.title: Kansas City Wiz / Kansas City Wizards — FunWhileItLasted

stadium_history_facts: Groundbreaking 11 July 1968; the stadium opened 12 August 1972 (Chiefs beat the St. Louis Cardinals 24–14 in the first preseason game) as part of the Truman Sports Complex, which it shares with Kauffman Stadium (home of MLB's Royals).
Originally designed by Kansas City firm Kivett and Myers; the 2007–2010 renovation was designed by Populous (formerly HOK Sport) at a cost of about US$375 million.
Original capacity was 78,097 (1972–1994); current Chiefs-configuration capacity is 76,416 (2010–present).
Home of the Kansas City Chiefs (NFL) continuously since 1972.
Naming rights sold to GEHA in March 2021, making the official name 'GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium'.
Was home to MLS charter club the Kansas City Wiz/Wizards (now Sporting Kansas City) from 1996 to 2007.
Playing surface is NorthBridge Bermudagrass (natural grass), in use since 2013.
Holds the Guinness World Record for loudest crowd roar at a sports stadium — 142.2 dBA, set 29 September 2014 (Chiefs 41, Patriots 14).
For the 2026 FIFA World Cup it is rebranded 'Kansas City Stadium' and hosts six matches: four group-stage games, one Round of 32, and one quarterfinal.
